thread:
alex: Heads up — scheduling a 3h capacity-smoothing window in apac1 on Tue 2026-03-31 02:00-05:00 UTC. We'll rotate preemptible GPU cohorts and apply NIC microcode. Rolling cordon+drain per cohort, ~5-12m per node. No full pool outage expected. @maria @jyoti @sam please ack.
maria: Ack. Do we have an ops runbook link? :eyes:
alex: Runbook: https://internal/runbooks/apac-capacity-smoothing — includes cohort order + rollback steps.
jyoti: Backfill plan? We currently have 4 reserved nodes in apac1-reserved. If pressure spikes we can briefly backfill from eu-west (will incur egress). Propose to prefer local reserved first.
sam: Product question — Hosted API SLO exposure? Any expected tail impact for large-gen requests?
alex: Expect short tail increases (1-3s) for a handful of large-gen flows during the node move, ~10m windows. We'll enable automatic fallback to smaller quantized model on overflow and use prefix cache to minimize regen.
leo: Cost shout — cross-region backfill egress could add up. Rough estimate for a full eu->apac burst is $1.2k. Can we reduce that?
alex: Yes. Plan B: increase stagger between cohorts to 30m and force warmup jobs so cache hitrate stays high. That should cut cross-region spill by ~80%.
sched-bot: Maintenance scheduled by alex for apac1 on 2026-03-31T02:00:00Z — cohorts: A,B,C,D. Notifying oncall 01:45 UTC.
maria: Checklist: 1) customer notice? 2) client retry bump? 3) canary route set? 4) alert suppression configured? Need owners.
alex: 1) Status page PR queued — will post notice 12h prior. 2) We'll bump internal client retries for 15m backoff window. 3) Canary route -> eu-west is ready. 4) I'll create transient SLO alert suppression during the window.
jyoti: Cordoning/drain commands (for runbook):
```
kubectl cordon node-{{NODE}}
kubectl drain node-{{NODE}} --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
alex: Also will launch KV cache pre-warm job 30m before each cohort start.
sam: Product will run smoke canary queries when each cohort finishes to validate quality.
leo: I'm ok with cost if we cap egress at $800 via throttles. Reduce eu backfill to final fallback only.
maria: Oncall — @sam @jyoti @alex — who is primary at run time?
sam: I'll be available first hour, then on standby.
jyoti: I'm on for the full window.
alex: I'll lead the operation and post updates. Plan: start cohort-A at 02:00, then A->B->C->D with 30m staggers. Post status every 30m. I'll escalate if any node fails to drain within 20m.
incident-bot: Created incident INC-20260331-01 (scheduled maintenance) — https://incidents/internal/INC-20260331-01
alex: Final note — if we detect abnormal regen rate >3x baseline after a cohort, abort remaining cohorts and revert routing. :thumbsup:
maria: Thanks. I'll prep the postmortem template and capture metrics to collect.
